facts.text: Model risk combines how much a simulation's output drives a decision (model influence) with the severity of a wrong decision (decision consequence), and determines how much credibility evidence the simulation needs.
facts.quote: Model risk is how much a simulation's output drives a decision (its influence) combined with how severe a wrong decision would be (the consequence), and it sets how much credibility evidence the simulation must have.

facts.text: The medical-device standard ASME V&V 40, issued by the American Society of Mechanical Engineers in 2018, defines model risk as the combination of model influence and decision consequence.
facts.quote: The medical-device standard ASME V&V 40 (American Society of Mechanical Engineers, 2018) defines model risk as the combination of two things.

facts.text: A simulation that is the only evidence for whether a 100 t machine stops before a person has very high model risk.
facts.quote: A model that is the only evidence for whether a 100 t machine stops before a person has very high model risk [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Model risk is rated using a grid with low, medium and high model influence on one axis and low, medium and high decision consequence on the other, rather than a formula with units.
facts.quote: The rating is a grid, not a formula with units: low, medium and high influence on one axis, low, medium and high consequence on the other.

facts.text: The model-risk grid position sets credibility goals agreed in advance for verification thoroughness, validation closeness and knowledge of inputs; these goals increase with risk.
facts.quote: The position sets credibility goals, agreed in advance, for each kind of evidence: how thorough verification must be, how close validation must come, how well inputs must be known. Goals rise with risk

facts.text: The space agency standard uses a criticality assessment to make the same risk-based credibility decision as the model-risk grid.
facts.quote: The space agency standard makes the same move with a criticality assessment

facts.text: The European automated-vehicle regulation requires a criticality assessment.
facts.quote: the European automated-vehicle regulation requires one [Chapter 10].

facts.text: For the collision-mitigation validation program, the booklet judges the physical brake model probably to be the highest-risk model in the chain because brake behavior varies with wear and temperature and has the highest decision consequence.
facts.quote: the physical brake model is probably the highest-risk model in the chain, because brake behavior varies with wear and temperature and has the highest decision consequence

facts.text: For the collision-mitigation validation program, sensor models in dust, darkness and glare have high model risk because they are the least validated models.
facts.quote: sensor models in dust, darkness and glare are high risk because they are least validated.

facts.text: A combinatorial sweep over site layouts and speeds carries lower model risk because the sweep exercises validated physics many times.
facts.quote: A combinatorial sweep over site layouts and speeds exercises validated physics many times and carries lower model risk [Chapter 10].

facts.text: No framework prescribes a universal percentage of physical tests or a universal tolerance; mature practice derives both from model influence, decision consequence, applicability and uncertainty.
facts.quote: No framework prescribes a universal percentage of physical tests or a universal tolerance; mature practice derives both from model influence, decision consequence, applicability and uncertainty

facts.text: Physical testing is retained where model risk is high and validation evidence is weakest.
facts.quote: physical testing is kept where model risk is high and validation evidence weakest [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Rating the model risk of each claim provides a defensible basis for splitting testing between simulation and physical tests.
facts.quote: Rating each claim's model risk is the honest route to a defensible test split.
